simple.meaning: מַחֲרֵשָׁה (machărêshâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “probably a pick-axe.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 13:20. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַחֲרֵשָׁה (H4281).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַחֲרֵשָׁה (machărêshâh) / H4281 is traced through 1 Samuel 13:20, 1 Samuel 13:21 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4281. machareshah [ מַחֲרֶ֫שֶׁת מַחֲרֵשָׁה, ] noun feminine ploughshare — singular suffix מַחֲרַשְׁתּוֺ אִישׁ לִלְטוֺשׁ 1Sam 8:20 to sharpen each man his ploughshare 13:20 (+ קַרְדֻּמּוֺ אֵתוֺ, ) + מַחֲרֵשָׁתוֺ 13:20 , read probably דָּרְבָּנוֺ his goad (so ᵑ6 ᵐ5 We Dr, see 13:21 ); plural absolute מַחֲרֵשֹׁת 13:21 (+ similar list; on text of both verses see Dr).

occurrences.englishText: but all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his own plowshare, mattock, ax, and sickle.
The price was one payim† A payim (or pim) was 2/3 shekel of silver, or 0.26 ounces, or 7.6 grams each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
